name: Critical minerals
value: Rare-earth pause extended to early Jan 2027
summary: China extended its pause on some rare-earth export controls by two months on 9 Nov; April 2025 licensing stays
state: On 9 Nov China extended by two months its pause on rare-earth export controls that was due to end that day, alongside a US extension of tariff exclusions and port-fee suspensions to 10 Jan 2027 (Thompson Hine, 13 Nov). Controls imposed in April 2025 on seven heavy rare earths remain in force, and the IEA estimates full controls could put $6.5tn of annual downstream output outside China at risk (The National, 16 Nov). No production stoppages outside China linked to export bans were found as of 17 Nov, so Watch holds.
for_you: Manufacturers of magnets, electric vehicles, electronics and defence equipment are most exposed to licensing delays. No consumer shortages have been reported.
rubric_hit: Watch: export licensing on seven rare earths in force since Apr 2025; no reported stoppages outside China for Alert

why: Rare earths, gallium, germanium and graphite are chokepoints for chips, EVs and defence — and China dominates processing.
drivers: Export controls, trade disputes, mine outages, stockpiling.
